text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet raised petrol prices by 20-21 percent and diesel fuel prices by 26 percent, effective from December 10, because of the sharp fall of the lev against the dollar on the local forex market. @
-- Bulgaria must pass law amendments required for the introduction of a currency board system by February and dissolve by March, main opposition Union of Democratic Forces leader Ivan Kostov said.
-- Two International Monetary Fund's (IMF) missions are expected to arrive in Bulgaria after December 11 to discuss the planned introduction of a currency board system, IMF officials in Sofia said.
-- Bulgaria's central government budget deficit totalled 155.4 billion levs on November 30, or 192.5 percent of the annual target in the unrevised budget, Finance Ministry figures showed.
-- Bulgaria's gross domestic product could rise by 10 percent in 1997 if a currency board system is introduced in the country in January, Prime minister Zhan Videnov said.
-- Bulgaria's Health ministry owes three billion levs to suppliers of medicines and pharmaceutical products, a Medicine Suppliers Chamber official said. @
-- Bulgaria's Telecommunications Company (BTC) said it had signed a $5.7 million contract with Hewlett Packard to buy communication equipment and software for BTC.
-- Romania lifted the ban on meat imports from Bulgaria after an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease in southeastern Bulgaria was eliminated, state news agency BTA said.
-- The European Commission said it would extend 20 million Ecus for social payments to Bulgaria under a request from Bulgaria's president-elect Petar Stoyanov. @
-- Bulgaria is expected to finalise the sale of a 60 percent stake of its soda ash producer Sodi Devnya by the end of the week, Prime Minister Zhan Videnov said.
-- Bulgaria posted 51 billion levs trade surplus in the third qarter of 1996, National Statistics Institute figures showed.
